title: Untitled
altText: An abstract painting of overlapping, multicolored rings and circles, with looser brushstrokes draping across them like winding thread.

source.verifiedBy: Art Institute of Chicago API record: title, artist (Tanaka Atsuko, Japanese, 1932-2005), date, medium, dimensions, credit line, style (Gutai group), is_public_domain false and the museum's image alt text read from the record

context: Tanaka Atsuko (1932 to 2005) was a Japanese artist associated with the Gutai group. This untitled enamel-on-canvas painting from 1964 measures about 90.5 by 72.5 centimeters, and the Art Institute describes it as overlapping, multicolored rings and circles with looser brushstrokes draping across them like winding thread.

descriptions.k: Look at all the circles! Rings in many colors sit on top of each other. Loose lines wind across them like long thread. Can you find a ring inside another ring? Which circle do you like most?
descriptions.g12: Tanaka Atsuko was an artist from Japan. She painted many rings and circles in different colors. They overlap like a tangle. Loose, curvy lines wind across them like thread. Where do the circles start and stop? Which color stands out to you?
descriptions.g35: Tanaka Atsuko was a Japanese artist who belonged to the Gutai group, whose members tried new and surprising ways of making art. In this untitled painting from 1964, colorful rings and circles overlap, and looser brushstrokes wind across them like thread. There are no objects, only line, color, and shape. How do the circles seem to connect, and what path would your eyes take?
descriptions.g68: Tanaka Atsuko painted this untitled work in 1964 using enamel on canvas. The museum describes overlapping, multicolored rings and circles, with looser brushstrokes draped across them like winding thread. She belonged to the Gutai group, a Japanese avant-garde group known for experimenting with materials and actions. Notice how the circles overlap and link, and how looser brushwork adds movement. Some viewers may think of networks or connections, though the painting does not name a subject.
descriptions.g910: In this untitled 1964 painting, Tanaka Atsuko builds a field of overlapping, multicolored rings and circles, crossed by looser brushstrokes that the Art Institute compares to winding thread. As a member of the Gutai group, she belonged to a Japanese avant-garde that valued experiment and individuality. The enamel paint and the rhythm of repeated rings give the surface a charged, vibrating quality. With no title or subject to guide us, viewers must decide how to read the relationships among line, color, and circle.
descriptions.g1112: Tanaka Atsuko's untitled painting of 1964, in enamel on canvas, presents overlapping multicolored rings and circles with looser, thread-like strokes draped across them. As a member of the Gutai group, she worked within a postwar Japanese avant-garde that prized experimentation and the individuality of materials and gestures. The painting's density and linked forms invite associations with networks, circuitry, or bodies, but the record offers no interpretation, so such readings remain speculative. Its untitled status shifts responsibility for meaning to the viewer and to what the surface itself shows.

teacherNote.context: An untitled 1964 enamel painting by Tanaka Atsuko (1932 to 2005), a member of the Gutai group, a Japanese avant-garde group. The museum describes overlapping multicolored rings and circles with loose thread-like strokes.
directions: Have students fill a page with overlapping circles in different colors, then add loose connecting lines, and describe the effect.
Ask students to give the painting three possible titles and explain how each changes their reading.
Discuss what it means for artists to form a group to experiment together.
